messages:
sara: Heads-up — scheduling a maintenance window for az2 GPU pool next Tue 02:00–05:00 UTC. thermal sensor firmware patch + NIC microcode. We'll do cohorted soft reboots and node drains, aim for zero customer-visible API 5xx but expect brief tail-latency spikes.

miguel: ETA on start? and which pools exactly?

osps-bot: (automated) new maintenance created: id mnt-az2-20260324 — assigned to oncall team.

sara: Start 02:00 UTC, target pool is az2-gpu-pool (all racks in az2), cohort size = 8 nodes at a time, ~12 cohorts. We'll cordon, drain user pods, run firmware, reboot, verify kernel & NIC health, then uncordon.

rahul: Any Dedicated customers pinned to az2 that need manual migration?

sara: Good call — check routing table for reserved capacity. I ran a quick query: two dedicated contracts with pinned nodes in az2 (tenant ids t-132, t-199). We'll contact account owners and offer temporary failover to az1 during window.

jen: Risk: if a cohort reprovision backfill hits capacity shortfall we should throttle API ingress, otherwise queues pile. Can we pre-warm burst pool in az1?

miguel: We can spin up a 24h burst pool with spot GPUs in az1 for backfill. Cost estimate ~ $6k for the window if fully used, but should be much less.

sara: Action: miguel to provision burst pool + test routing by EOD Fri. rahul to notify the two account owners and post PSAT tickets. jen to update autoscaler with cohort-aware limits. kai to own post-maint health checks.

kai: For verification, I want the following checks after each cohort uncordon: 1) per-GPU temp < 78C for 10m, 2) NVLink/PCIe error counters zero, 3) p95 latency for small-gen under 250ms. I'll post a Prometheus query snippet.

kai: ```
avg_over_time(gpu_temp_c{pool="az2-gpu-pool"}[10m]) < 78
sum(rate(nvlink_errors_total{job="gpu-driver"}[1m])) == 0
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gen_latency_bucket{route="small-gen"}[5m])) by (le)) < 0.25
```

miguel: Nice. Also add a NVMe SMART quick check after reboot: `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 | grep -E "(critical|media)"` in the runbook.

natalie-sales: FYI — I'll prep a short customer comms blur for any customers who ask about scheduled infra work. Need copy by Mon AM.

jen: Can we do a single canary cohort at 01:00 UTC (1 hour earlier) with synthetic load to validate patch? prefer earlier to reduce risk.

sara: Yes — canary cohort at 01:00, will run 30m of synthetic load (open-source perf harness). If canary fails, pause and rollback firmware for remainder.

miguel: Rollback plan: firmware revert + node reboot to prepatch image. We'll tag images `prepatch-20260324` and `postpatch-20260324`. Keep 4 spare nodes unpatched for emergency failover.

rahul: On-call rota: sara (lead), miguel (infra), kai (telemetry), jen (autoscaler). Ops-bot will escalate to oncall@redwood if cohort health falls below threshold.

ops-bot: (automated) maintenance mnt-az2-20260324 scheduled. Reminders set: 24h, 2h, 15m.

sara: Runbook excerpt (for whoever executes):
```
1) cordon nodes: `kubectl cordon <node>`
2) drain gracefully: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`
3) apply firmware: `fw-updater apply --package sensor-nic-1.4.2`
4) reboot: `sudo systemctl reboot`
5) post checks: run kai's PromQL checks, NVMe SMART, kernel dmesg scan for 'PCIe' or 'nvlink' errors`
```

jen: Put a temporary fallback routing rule to divert <5% traffic to az1 if p95 > 750ms for 3 consecutive cohorts. We'll automate with routing controller.

miguel: Also ensure console shows maintenance banner and read-only mode for rollout config during window to avoid conflicts.

natalie-sales: Draft comms: "Planned maintenance in az2 on Mar 24 02:00–05:00 UTC. We expect no customer-facing outages but may see brief latency spikes. Contact support if you rely on pinned Dedicated nodes." Will share draft.

rahul: Anything else? backups, logs retention?

sara: Take ephemeral snapshots of any local stateful pods before drain (rare) — add `kubectl snapshot` step. Logs: increase debug retention for mng-plane and driver logs for 6h post-maint.

miguel: I'll run a cost calc once burst pool sizing is set and post here. Estimated worst-case $6k, expected < $1k.

jen: Approved by infra leads. Proceed with canary + main. Please stick to the runbook and escalate early. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: (automated) reminder posted 24h prior to start: Mar 23 02:00 UTC.

sara: Thanks all — I'll update the maintenance ticket and link this thread. If anything blocks, ping me with @sara.
